title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous (biallelic) mutation in the DST gene (113810) on chromosome 6p12.1.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous (biallelic) mutation in the DST gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We now report an inherited skin fragility disorder with a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST) that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1, BPAG1-e (also known as BP230).
checks.explanation: Paper reports a single homozygous mutation; compound heterozygous/biallelic and the 'localized or generalized intermediate' subtype naming are not in the abstract.

checks.claim: The DST gene is located on chromosome 6p12.1.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST)
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene named in the paper; the abstract itself does not state 6p12.1.

paragraphs.text: EBS3 is an autosomal recessive form of epidermolysis bullosa simplex. It is caused by mutations in DST, which encodes an epithelial isoform of dystonin, BPAG1-e (BP230) (Ganani et al., 2021; Groves et al., 2010). The skin is fragile, with blisters and erosions that arise after trauma or spontaneously (Groves et al., 2010).

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) reported a 38-year-old man with an inherited skin fragility disorder. Throughout his life he had had generalized blisters and erosions, induced by trauma or arising spontaneously, especially around the ankles. Beginning at age 37 years he had episodes of numbness in his limbs. He had also been diagnosed with CADASIL, and the authors noted that this made it harder to tell whether the neurologic symptoms were due to the DST mutation.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) found a homozygous DST mutation in an affected man and concluded that the disorder is autosomal recessive. Liu et al. (2012) also reported autosomal recessive EBS due to loss of BPAG1-e expression. Ganani et al. (2021) stated that DST-associated EBS is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) studied a 38-year-old man with autosomal recessive EBS. They identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the DST gene, gln1124-to-ter (Q1124X), which lies in the region encoding the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230). In the patient's skin, the mutation led to loss of the hemidesmosomal inner plaques and complete absence of BPAG1-e immunostaining. Immunolabeling for plectin, beta-4 integrin, and type XVII collagen was reduced. The authors concluded that BPAG1-e pathology underlies a new form of autosomal recessive EBS.

paragraphs.text: Ganani et al. (2021) studied 5 patients with EBS from 3 families. Using whole-exome and direct sequencing, they identified biallelic mutations in the DST gene. Two of the variants had not been reported before: c.7097dupA (Y2366X) and c.7429delC, which causes a frameshift (Leu2477SerfsTer13).

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) studied a 38-year-old man with autosomal recessive EBS who had lifelong generalized blisters and erosions. In this patient they identified a homozygous gln1124-to-ter (Q1124X) nonsense mutation in the DST gene, in the region encoding the coiled-coil domain of BPAG1-e. The patient's skin had lost its hemidesmosomal inner plaques and showed complete absence of BPAG1-e immunostaining. Labeling for plectin, beta-4 integrin, and type XVII collagen was reduced.
